lawyer: S.R. Pal, Sr. Advocate, instructed by Abu Bakkar, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Appellants.
parties:
Abu Ahmed Abdul Hafiz and others ------ Petitioner
Vs.
M.A. Hoque Shirajee ------ Respondent
full_judgment: 4. Mr. S.R. Pal, learned Advocate for the appellants has seriously assailed the impugned order of the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division contenting that it is unwarranted by law and fact and that it is unjust and improper causing grave injustice to the appellants who have been deprived of the fruits of their decree without being given any opportunity to be heard in the matter. As has been stated above, the decree for ejectment as well as for realisation of a huge arrear of rent on the ground of default in the payment of rent, passed by the trial court on 6 May 1967, was challenged by the respondent at all stages and forums without any success and the decree was maintained as one having been passed in accordance with law. Thereafter, when the decree was sought to be executed an attempt was made by the respondent-tenant to get the execution proceeding struck off by deliberate misrepresentation that the decree had been otherwise adjusted, and when that attempt failed, the respondent filed the independent suit for a declaration that the decree for ejectment was void and illegal. The respondent may proceed with his suits, if so advised, but there is no reason whatsoever why the execution of the decree which was obtained in 1967 in a different suit should be stayed when the said decree was maintained all through. Mere filing of a suit, particularly in the circumstances as narrated above, confers no right upon the respondent for asking for stay of the execution of the decree. Both the trial court and the first revisional court, namely the Additional District Judge, observed that the respondent-tenant was making deliberate obstruction to execution of the decree for ejectment by filing the application for stay of execution of the decree. The learned Additional District Judge further observed that stay of a proceeding is discretion of the court and that when that discretion was exercised in this case by the trial court on sound judicial principle, revisional court got no jurisdiction to interfere. The learned Single Judge has observed that execution of the decree will seriously prejudice the judgment-debtor, plaintiff. There can hardly be any question raised as to prejudice to the judgment debtor when a lawful decree is put into execution. Moreover, disposal of the revisional application on merits giving the relief sought for resulted in the reversal of the order of the Additional District Judge without hearing the opposite party. This is illegal, unfair, unjust and improper. We strongly disapprove of disposal of revisional applications in this manner.
